For estate and letting agents

Social media for estate and letting agents

Your listings live on the portals, but your social media shows sellers and landlords who you are. Here is what to post through the year, the material information rules for property posts, and how Kanosena can write a week of posts from your own website for you to approve.

Request early access See an example week

Free while we test with our first businesses. Nothing is posted until you approve it.

What’s worth posting

Posts that win valuations and instructions, not just likes.

  • New listings and price changes

    Include the price or rent, the council tax band and the tenure, so the post works as a proper listing.

  • Sold and let agreed

    A simple “sold” or “let agreed” post shows you are busy. Never share buyers’ or tenants’ details.

  • Local area guides

    Schools, parks, transport, the high street. Help people picture living there.

  • Market updates

    Plain-English updates on what is happening locally, using figures you can source.

  • Meet the team

    Who will value the home, show buyers round and answer the phone.

  • Tips for sellers and landlords

    Getting ready for viewings, what an EPC is, what landlords need to know when rules change.

Your year at a glance

Moments in the UK calendar worth planning posts around.

January
New year, new move. People start looking and booking valuations.
March to May
Gardens look their best: good for listings, valuations and moving guides.
June to August
Families want to move before the new school year starts in September.
September to November
The last chance to move before Christmas. Use your own figures on how long sales are taking.
December
Office hours over Christmas, and a look back at your year.
When rules change
Changes to Stamp Duty or to renting law (such as the Renters’ Rights Act in England) are good moments for a clear explainer.

Rules worth knowing

Social media posts are advertising, so the usual rules apply. These are the ones that come up most in your line of work.

  • Property posts need material information

    National Trading Standards says agents must not leave material information out of property listings. “Part A” information (the price or rent, the council tax band or rate, and tenure for sales) is always material. Treat a post about a specific property as a listing, and include these there too.

    Material information guidance (National Trading Standards)

  • Reviews must be real

    The Digital Markets, Competition and Consumers Act 2024 bans fake reviews and publishing reviews in a misleading way, such as hiding negative ones. Share genuine reviews, with the client’s permission.

    Reviews and endorsements (Business Companion)

  • Back up every claim

    “Number one agent in town” or “we sell in half the time” needs evidence you can show. Claims you can’t back up count as misleading advertising.

  • Protect clients’ privacy

    Don’t share details about buyers, tenants or agreed prices that your clients haven’t agreed to share.

General information, checked on 27/11/2026. It isn’t legal advice: check with the body named for your own situation.

How Kanosena helps

You approve. We handle the rest.

  • We read your websiteWe build a short profile of your business, and every fact shows where it came from. You can edit any of it.
  • We write your weekPosts and simple branded graphics in your colours, written only from your profile, with UK dates and seasons in mind.

  • We post and report backApproved posts go out to your Facebook Page, Instagram business account or LinkedIn Page, and we show you how they did.

Questions

Do you replace the property portals?

No. The portals are where buyers and tenants search. Kanosena keeps your own Facebook, Instagram and LinkedIn pages active with posts you approve.

Will you make claims about our results?

No. Posts are written from what your own website says. We don’t invent figures, reviews or awards.

Do you post to LinkedIn too?

Yes. We post to LinkedIn Pages as well as Facebook Pages and Instagram business accounts, so landlords and local businesses see you as well as home movers.
